checklist.step: Pull the CMS CSR variant specification for the plan year
actions: Open the CMS Plan Management Community / Actuary Value Calculator and download the current CSR variant AV levels (94%, 87%, 73% and standard 70%) for silver metal.
Record each variant's target deductible, copay, coinsurance and MOOP ranges from the AV Calculator output.
Hand the spec package to the Configuration Engineer with the target plan year and effective date.
checklist.done: the CSR variant spec (AV levels, cost-sharing ranges, effective date) is handed to Configuration Engineer with a dated source capture.

checklist.step: Build the CSR plan-variant codes in the policy admin system
actions: In PolicyCenter open Product Designer ▸ Plan Configuration and create variant plan codes 02/03/04 nested under the base silver product, plus the standard non-CSR variant.
Enter deductible, copay, coinsurance and MOOP field values for each variant from the actuarial memo, not the AV Calculator estimate.
Save the build as a versioned product model and route it to QA.
checklist.done: all CSR variant codes exist in Plan Configuration with cost-sharing fields matching the actuarial memo.

checklist.step: Confirm the configured values reconcile to the certified actuarial memorandum
actions: Compare each field in the Plan Configuration build to the SERFF-filed actuarial memorandum and AV certification for that variant.
Flag and return to Configuration Engineer any field that does not match the certified value.
Sign the configuration validation form once all fields tie out.
checklist.done: every configured cost-sharing field matches the certified actuarial memorandum, with a signed validation form.

checklist.step: Map the 834 CSR eligibility-category indicator to the correct plan variant
actions: In the 834 enrollment processor, map the inbound CSR eligibility-category code (loop 2000, REF segment) to the internal plan-variant field.
Route any 834 with a missing or invalid CSR indicator to a manual exception queue instead of defaulting to standard cost-sharing.
Document the segment-to-field mapping in the integration spec.
checklist.done: the 834 processor assigns the correct variant from the CSR indicator and routes invalid indicators to the exception queue.

checklist.step: Unit test each variant's cost-sharing values against the actuarial memo
actions: Build one test case per CSR variant covering deductible, copay, coinsurance and MOOP accumulation.
Run each case in the test environment and compare system output field-by-field to the actuarial memo.
Log any discrepancy as a defect against the Configuration Engineer.
checklist.done: unit test results match the actuarial memo for every variant with zero open defects.

checklist.step: Run an end-to-end test from 834 enrollment through claims pricing
actions: Submit one test 834 per CSR income band (100-150%, 150-200%, 200-250% FPL) and the standard band through the full enrollment-to-billing stack.
Confirm the enrollee lands on the correct variant plan code in the policy record.
Submit a test claim for each enrollee and confirm the claims platform prices cost-sharing off the assigned variant, not the base plan.
checklist.done: each CSR income band's test enrollee is priced at claims adjudication using the correct variant's cost-sharing.

checklist.step: Validate claims adjudication accumulators track by variant
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: In ClaimCenter open the benefit accumulator for a sampled CSR test member and confirm deductible/MOOP accumulation uses the variant's thresholds.
Confirm a mid-year CSR category change re-points the accumulator to the new variant without resetting improperly.
Record findings on the test summary.
checklist.done: accumulators track against the correct variant thresholds, including on a mid-year CSR category change.

checklist.step: Configure and test the manual exception queue for unmatched CSR indicators
actions: Confirm the exception queue in the enrollment processor surfaces every 834 with a missing/invalid CSR indicator with the member id and state.
Work each queued item to resolution by confirming the correct CSR category with the exchange or the member file, within a 2-business-day SLA.
Log the resolution and re-run the 834 to apply the corrected variant.
checklist.done: the exception queue catches unmatched CSR indicators and each is resolved within the 2-business-day SLA.

checklist.step: Document the configuration and the 834 mapping logic
actions: Write the configuration spec covering variant codes, field values and the 834-to-variant mapping table.
Version and publish the spec in Confluence under the plan-year CSR build page.
Link the spec to the actuary sign-off and QA test results.
checklist.done: a versioned configuration spec exists in Confluence, linked to actuary sign-off and test evidence.

checklist.step: Obtain Compliance approval of the configuration before go-live
actions: Review the configuration spec and test results against 45 CFR 156.410, 156.420, 147.126 and 156.130.
Confirm the exception-queue SLA and accumulator behavior meet the no-annual/lifetime-limit and correct-CSR-application standard.
Sign the compliance approval field on the change record.
checklist.done: Compliance signs the configuration approval before the build is promoted.

checklist.step: Promote the configuration to production ahead of the September 30 freeze
actions: Open a change record referencing the signed configuration spec and schedule the production migration date.
Confirm the migration date lands before September 30 to precede the plan-year Open Enrollment build freeze.
Obtain change approval and execute the migration in the release window.
checklist.done: the CSR configuration is live in production before the September 30 freeze, under an approved change record.

checklist.step: Set daily reconciliation monitoring for CSR misclassification
actions: Configure a daily report comparing each enrollee's CSR eligibility category on the enrollment file to the plan variant applied in the policy record.
Route any mismatch to the Policy Administration Analyst exception queue same day.
Confirm the report runs and alerts on schedule for one full cycle before relying on it.
checklist.done: a daily CSR reconciliation report is running and routing mismatches to the exception queue.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any configuration defects found post-go-live
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each CSR misclassification found via the daily reconciliation or a complaint, with member id and affected claims.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Confirm affected claims are reprocessed at the correct cost-sharing and the member is made whole.
checklist.done: every found misclassification has a logged issue, root cause, owner and confirmed member remediation.

checklist.step: Confirm the Appointed Actuary re-certifies AV for any mid-year change
actions: Review any change request that alters CSR variant cost-sharing values mid-plan-year.
Re-run the AV Calculator to confirm the change keeps each variant within its CMS AV band.
Sign or reject the change before it reaches Configuration Engineer.
checklist.done: no mid-year CSR cost-sharing change is built without a dated actuary AV re-certification.

checklist.step: Retain the configuration and test evidence for the plan year
actions: Move the configuration spec, test results, actuary sign-off and compliance approval into the compliance evidence repository under the plan year.
Apply the 7-year-from-plan-year-retirement retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by plan year and variant code.
checklist.done: the CSR configuration record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by plan year.

testing.step: Build the population of CSR-eligible enrollees for the test period
actions: Extract all active silver-level individual QHP enrollees carrying a CSR eligibility category from the policy admin system as of the test date.
Reconcile the extract count to the exchange enrollment reconciliation file for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before drawing the sample.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the exchange enrollment file and signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take a seeded random sample of 40 enrollees stratified across the four CSR income bands and the standard variant.
Add any enrollee flagged by the daily reconciliation report during the period.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn and documented.

testing.step: Independently re-derive the correct CSR variant for each sampled enrollee
actions: From the exchange eligibility file, read each sampled enrollee's income band and CSR eligibility category without looking at the assigned plan record first.
Compare your derived variant to the variant assigned in the policy record.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled enrollee has an independently derived variant compared to the system-assigned variant.

testing.step: Re-perform the claims cost-share calculation for each sampled enrollee
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Pull one adjudicated claim per sampled enrollee from ClaimCenter and recompute deductible/copay/coinsurance using the actuarial memo's variant values.
Compare the recomputed cost-sharing to what the system actually charged the member.
Log any difference as an exception with the dollar impact.
testing.done: recomputed cost-sharing matches the amount actually applied for every sampled claim, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the 834 exception queue handling for the sample period
actions: Pull every 834 that landed in the CSR exception queue during the test period.
Confirm each was resolved within the 2-business-day SLA and re-run to apply the corrected variant.
Flag any item resolved late or left unresolved.
testing.done: every exception-queue item in the period is confirmed resolved within SLA or logged as late.

testing.step: Recompute AV bands for the sampled variants
actions: Independently re-run the CMS AV Calculator for each sampled variant's configured cost-sharing values.
Confirm the result falls within the CMS-permitted AV band for that CSR level.
Log any variant that falls outside its band as a breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled variant's recomputed AV falls within its CMS band, or is logged as a breach.

testing.step: Confirm the change-management trail for the plan-year build
actions: Pull the change record for the plan-year CSR configuration and confirm actuary sign-off and Compliance approval both pre-date the production migration.
Confirm the migration date is on or before September 30.
Flag any late or unsigned promotion.
testing.done: the change record shows actuary and Compliance sign-off before a pre-September-30 migration, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Check accumulator behavior on a mid-year CSR category change
actions: Select any sampled enrollee with a mid-year CSR category change and pull the accumulator history before and after the change.
Confirm the accumulator re-points to the new variant's thresholds without an improper reset.
Log any incorrect accumulator behavior as an exception.
testing.done: accumulator behavior on mid-year changes is confirmed correct for every sampled instance, or logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the member id, variant discrepancy and dollar impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date including member reprocessing where cost-sharing was wrong.
Carry any open exception into the next test cycle as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on wrong-variant cost-sharing.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Define the in-scope role roster for the training cycle
actions: Pull the current staff list for Configuration Engineering, Policy Administration, Claims and Product roles that touch CSR eligibility or EHB limits from the HRIS org roster.
Cross-check against system access lists for the policy admin and claims platforms to catch anyone with access outside the HR role list.
Publish the roster to the Learning & Development Specialist as the assignment source.
checklist.done: a reconciled roster of every in-scope staff member is handed to Learning & Development for assignment.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum content for the current CMS guidance
actions: Compare the existing course content to the current 45 CFR 156.410/420, 147.126 and 156.130 text and any new CMS bulletin.
Draft content updates covering CSR variant assignment, EHB annual/lifetime limit prohibition and MLR notice handling.
Route the updated content to Compliance Manager for approval before publishing.
checklist.done: curriculum content reflects the current regulatory text with dated approval before publication.

checklist.step: Build the course and quiz in the LMS
actions: In Cornerstone LMS open Course Catalog ▸ Create Course and load the approved ACA/PHSA module content and scenario examples.
Attach a 10-question knowledge check with an 80% pass mark tied to CSR variant assignment and EHB limit scenarios.
Set the course version number and effective date.
checklist.done: the course and quiz are live in Cornerstone LMS with a versioned, dated release.

checklist.step: Configure automatic assignment rules for the roster
actions: In Cornerstone LMS open Assignment Rules and target the in-scope role roster by job code/org unit.
Set the due date to September 30 and enable automatic assignment for new hires entering an in-scope role mid-cycle.
Enable the T-30/T-14/T-3 reminder notifications and manager escalation on overdue status.
checklist.done: assignment rules cover the full roster including mid-cycle new hires, with reminders enabled.

checklist.step: Deliver the training and track completion
actions: Confirm each assigned learner accesses the module and completes the quiz with a passing score in the LMS transcript.
Follow up directly with any learner overdue past the T-3 reminder.
Pull a weekly completion status report and share it with each people manager.
checklist.done: a weekly completion report is produced and shared with managers throughout the cycle.

checklist.step: Escalate non-completion ahead of the September 30 deadline
actions: At T-3 days, pull the outstanding-completion list from the LMS and email each manager directly.
Escalate any name still outstanding at the deadline to the manager's own manager and to Compliance Officer.
Record the escalation and its outcome on the roster tracker.
checklist.done: every outstanding completion at deadline has a recorded escalation and outcome.

checklist.step: Restrict system access for staff who miss the deadline
actions: Pull the final non-completion list from the LMS at close of September 30.
Suspend CSR-configuration or claims cost-sharing write access in the IAM platform for anyone on the list.
Restore access on confirmed completion, logged with the completion date.
checklist.done: no staff member with write access to CSR configuration or claims cost-sharing lacks a current completion.

checklist.step: Verify no CSR-related transaction was processed by a non-completed staff member
actions: Cross-reference the transaction log (configuration changes, claims cost-share overrides) against the completion roster for the cycle.
Flag any transaction performed by a staff member without a current completion.
Route flagged transactions to Compliance Officer for review.
checklist.done: every CSR-related transaction in the cycle is matched to a staff member with a current completion, or flagged.

checklist.step: Log and disposition any flagged transaction
actions: Open a tracker issue for each flagged transaction with the staff member, transaction id and root cause (access gap, roster gap, LMS error).
Determine whether the underlying transaction itself was correct despite the training gap, and document the finding.
Set a remediation date and close only once the staff member has completed training.
checklist.done: every flagged transaction has a logged disposition and the staff member holds a completed training record.

checklist.step: Onboard new hires into the training cycle mid-year
actions: Notify Learning & Development within 5 business days of any new hire entering an in-scope role.
Confirm the LMS assignment rule auto-enrolled the new hire with a 30-day completion window from start date.
Track the new hire on the roster tracker separately from the annual cycle deadline.
checklist.done: every mid-year new hire is enrolled within 5 business days of start and tracked to a 30-day completion window.

checklist.step: Review quiz-failure patterns and remediate content gaps
actions: Pull the LMS quiz-item analysis report to identify questions with a high failure rate.
Revise course content or examples for any question failing more than 25% of learners.
Republish the updated course version and re-notify affected learners if content materially changed.
checklist.done: quiz items with a high failure rate are analyzed and the course content revised where warranted.

checklist.step: Document the curriculum approval trail
actions: Publish the approved curriculum content, version number and Head of Compliance approval date to the Compliance training page in Confluence.
Link the LMS course id to the Confluence record.
Archive the prior version with its retirement date.
checklist.done: the current curriculum version and its approval are published and linked to the LMS course id.

checklist.step: Report cycle completion status to the Compliance Committee
actions: Summarize final completion rate, outstanding names at deadline, access restrictions applied and flagged transactions.
Present the summary at the Compliance Committee's next sitting after the September 30 close.
Record the committee's acceptance or any directed follow-up action.
checklist.done: the Compliance Committee has received and accepted the cycle completion summary, with any follow-up action recorded.

checklist.step: Retain training evidence for the cycle
actions: Export the LMS completion report, quiz scores and curriculum version into the compliance evidence repository under the cycle year.
Apply the 5-year retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by staff member and cycle year.
checklist.done: training evidence for the cycle is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by staff member.

checklist.step: Set the next cycle's assignment date and curriculum review trigger
actions: Schedule the following year's assignment rule activation at least 60 days ahead of the September 30 deadline.
Set a calendar trigger to review CMS guidance for CSR/EHB changes 90 days before the next cycle opens.
Confirm the LMS assignment rule and reminder cadence carry forward unchanged unless the review finds a needed update.
checklist.done: the next cycle's assignment date and a pre-cycle regulatory review trigger are scheduled.

testing.step: Build the roster of staff required to complete training for the cycle
actions: Independently pull the in-scope role roster from HRIS and the IAM platform's access-by-role report as of September 30.
Reconcile this independently pulled roster to the roster Compliance used for LMS assignment.
List any name on the access list but missing from the assignment roster as an exception.
testing.done: the roster is independently reconciled to system access, with any gap logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of names flagged non-complete at the September 30 close.
Add a seeded random sample of 25 additional names from the completed population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all non-completions plus a documented random sample of completions.

testing.step: Verify each sampled completion in the LMS
actions: Open the LMS transcript for each sampled name and confirm a completed status with a passing quiz score and completion date.
Compare the completion date to the September 30 deadline and flag any completion recorded after the deadline.
Screenshot the transcript into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled completion is verified in the LMS transcript with a captured screenshot.

testing.step: Test access restriction enforcement for non-completions
actions: For every sampled non-completion, pull the IAM access log and confirm CSR-configuration or claims cost-sharing write access was suspended on September 30.
Confirm access was restored only after a dated completion record exists.
Log any account that retained access despite non-completion as an exception.
testing.done: access suspension and restoration timing is confirmed for every sampled non-completion, or logged.

testing.step: Trace transactions performed by sampled staff to their completion date
actions: Pull the CSR-related transaction log for each sampled staff member covering the cycle period.
Compare each transaction's date to the staff member's training completion date.
Log any transaction performed before completion as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled staff member's CSR transactions post-date their training completion, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the curriculum content check against current regulatory text
actions: Read 45 CFR 156.410, 156.420, 147.126 and 156.130 as currently published.
Compare the published course content in the LMS to the current text for accuracy and completeness.
Log any content gap or outdated reference as an exception for the next curriculum refresh.
testing.done: course content is confirmed current against the regulatory text, or a content gap is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the completion rate for the cycle
actions: Independently recompute completion rate as completions divided by the reconciled roster count.
Compare the recomputed rate to the rate reported to the Compliance Committee.
Log any difference as an exception requiring report correction.
testing.done: the recomputed completion rate matches the reported rate, or a correction is logged.

testing.step: Check mid-year new-hire enrollment timing
actions: Select every new hire who entered an in-scope role during the cycle from the HRIS new-hire report.
Confirm each was enrolled in the LMS within 5 business days of start date and completed within the 30-day window.
Log any late enrollment or completion as an exception.
testing.done: every mid-year new hire's enrollment and completion timing is confirmed, or logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the staff member, gap type and system(s) affected.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry any open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the 100% completion threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Capture every complaint at intake across all channels
actions: Log every complaint received via the Customer Self-Service Portal, contact center, producer or DOI referral into a CRM case within 1 business day.
Capture the member id, policy/plan variant, channel and verbatim complaint text on the case.
Route the case to the CSR/EHB triage queue if the complaint mentions cost-sharing amount, denied claim limit or plan variant.
checklist.done: every complaint received is logged as a CRM case within 1 business day, with channel and member id captured.

checklist.step: Tag the complaint with the correct CSR/EHB issue code
actions: In the CRM case, apply an issue code from the taxonomy: CSR-VARIANT-MISMATCH, EHB-LIMIT-APPLIED, MOOP-MISCALC or OTHER.
Attach the member's plan variant and the disputed claim or billing statement to the case.
Escalate ambiguous tagging to the Complaints Manager before proceeding.
checklist.done: every CSR/EHB-related complaint carries a taxonomy issue code and the disputed document attached.

checklist.step: Acknowledge the complaint within the 5-business-day standard
actions: Send the member or producer a written acknowledgment referencing the case number within 5 business days of intake.
Record the acknowledgment date on the CRM case.
Escalate any case approaching day 5 without acknowledgment to the Complaints Manager.
checklist.done: every case shows a recorded acknowledgment date within 5 business days of intake.

checklist.step: Investigate the CSR variant assignment underlying the complaint
actions: Pull the member's enrollment record and CSR eligibility category from the policy admin system.
Compare the assigned plan variant to the member's income-band eligibility category on file.
Record the finding (correct/incorrect assignment) on the CRM case with supporting screenshots.
checklist.done: the CSR variant assignment is verified against the eligibility category with evidence attached to the case.

checklist.step: Investigate any EHB annual/lifetime limit applied to a claim
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Pull the disputed claim in ClaimCenter and check whether any dollar limit, annual cap or lifetime cap was applied to an essential health benefit.
Confirm no such limit exists in the benefit configuration for that plan variant.
Record the finding on the CRM case.
checklist.done: the claim is checked for an improper EHB dollar limit and the finding is recorded on the case.

checklist.step: Determine root cause for every confirmed CSR/EHB error
actions: For every confirmed error, classify root cause as configuration defect, 834 mapping failure, manual processing error or member data error.
Check whether the same root cause appears on any other open or recently closed case.
Document the root cause finding on the case and in the trend log.
checklist.done: every confirmed error carries a documented root cause checked against other cases for a pattern.

checklist.step: Remediate the member's account and any affected claims
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Reprocess the disputed claim and any other claims for the member affected by the same error at the correct CSR variant or without the improper limit.
Issue any resulting refund or payment adjustment through the standard claims payment process.
Record the remediation amount and date on the CRM case.
checklist.done: the member's affected claims are reprocessed correctly with the remediation amount and date recorded.

checklist.step: Escalate a confirmed systemic issue to IT for a configuration fix
actions: Where root cause points to a configuration or mapping defect, open a ticket to the Configuration Engineer with the case reference and defect detail.
Request a population scan of other members who may share the same defect exposure.
Track the ticket to fix deployment and confirm closure references the fix.
checklist.done: a confirmed systemic issue has an IT ticket, a population scan requested, and tracked closure.

checklist.step: Scan for other affected members once a systemic issue is confirmed
actions: Query the enrollment and claims data warehouse for other members matching the same defect pattern (variant code, date range, plan).
Produce a list of affected members with the dollar impact per member.
Hand the list to Claims Adjuster for proactive remediation.
checklist.done: a population scan for the confirmed defect pattern is completed and handed off for remediation.

checklist.step: Close the case within the 30-day standard with a written resolution
actions: Send the member or producer a written resolution letter stating the finding and any remediation within 30 calendar days of intake.
Attach the resolution letter to the CRM case and set status to Closed.
Escalate any case that will miss the 30-day standard to the Complaints Manager before the deadline.
checklist.done: every case has a written resolution letter and a closed status within 30 calendar days, or a documented pre-deadline escalation.

checklist.step: Log the exception and disposition for every confirmed error
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each confirmed CSR/EHB error with root cause, member count affected and remediation status.
Determine whether the volume or nature of the issue triggers a self-report to the state DOI or CMS.
Sign off the disposition and file the self-report decision with Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: every confirmed error has a logged disposition and a documented self-report decision.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly CSR/EHB complaint trend report
actions: Pull closed CSR/EHB-tagged cases for the month from the CRM into the Power BI complaint dashboard.
Break out volume by issue code, root cause and average days-to-close.
Distribute the report to Compliance and Product leadership.
checklist.done: a monthly trend report by issue code and root cause is produced and distributed.

checklist.step: Review trend spikes with Product and IT for preventive action
actions: Review the monthly trend report for any issue code showing a month-over-month volume increase above 25%.
Convene Product and Configuration Engineering to determine a preventive fix or process change.
Track the preventive action to completion and confirm the trend reverses in the following cycle.
checklist.done: any trend spike has a preventive action tracked to completion with a confirmed volume reversal.

checklist.step: Confirm regulator-facing complaint reporting reflects CSR/EHB cases
actions: Confirm CSR/EHB-tagged complaints are correctly categorized in any NAIC MCAS or state complaint report submission.
Reconcile the complaint report count to the CRM case count for the same period.
Resolve any discrepancy before the report is submitted.
checklist.done: the regulator-facing complaint report count reconciles to the CRM case log before submission.

checklist.step: Retain complaint case evidence for the retention period
actions: Export the closed case file (intake, investigation, root cause, remediation, resolution letter) into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-close retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by member id and issue code.
checklist.done: the closed complaint case is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by member id and issue code.

testing.step: Build the population of CSR/EHB-tagged complaints closed in the quarter
actions: Extract every CRM case tagged CSR-VARIANT-MISMATCH, EHB-LIMIT-APPLIED or MOOP-MISCALC and closed in the quarter.
Reconcile the extract count to the monthly trend reports issued during the quarter.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the issued trend reports and signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of cases where a systemic issue was declared or a self-report decision was made.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 additional cases from the remaining population, minimum 30 total.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers all declared-systemic cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the CSR variant investigation for each sampled case
actions: Independently pull the member's eligibility category and assigned plan variant from the policy admin system.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the assignment was correct without reading the case's investigation notes first.
Compare to the recorded finding; log any difference as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent re-performance note compared to the recorded finding.

testing.step: Trace remediation to the claims payment system
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: For each sampled case with a confirmed error, pull the reprocessed claim and payment record in ClaimCenter.
Confirm the reprocessed amount matches the correct CSR variant or removes the improper EHB limit.
Confirm the payment date and amount tie to what was communicated to the member.
testing.done: reprocessed claim amounts and payments are traced and confirmed correct for every sampled error case.

testing.step: Test the acknowledgment and 30-day close SLA on the sample
actions: Compare each sampled case's acknowledgment date to intake date and resolution-letter date to intake date.
Flag any case breaching the 5-day acknowledgment or 30-day close standard.
Note any pattern of breaches by channel or issue code.
testing.done: SLA timing is confirmed or breached and logged for every sampled case.

testing.step: Verify the population scan for confirmed systemic issues
actions: For every sampled case declared systemic, pull the Data Quality Analyst's population scan output.
Independently re-query the data warehouse for the same defect pattern and compare member counts.
Log any member missed by the original scan as an exception requiring proactive remediation.
testing.done: the population scan for each systemic case is independently verified, with any missed member logged.

testing.step: Confirm self-report decisions were documented and cleared by counsel
actions: Review each sampled case where a self-report decision was made.
Confirm the decision rationale and, where a report was filed, the filing date and confirmation.
Log any case lacking a documented decision or counsel clearance as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled self-report decision is documented and counsel-cleared, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the trend report figures for the quarter
actions: Independently recompute complaint volume by issue code and root cause from the population extract.
Compare to the figures reported to Compliance and Product leadership.
Log any material difference as an exception requiring report correction.
testing.done: recomputed trend figures match the reported figures, or a correction is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the case id, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on missed close or unresolved root cause.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual audit of MLR rebate notice content and timing against the CMS-prescribed form

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 147.200 / PHSA 2715 (rebate notice requirement) and 45 CFR 158.251 (standardized notice content) re-read against the current CMS model notice template each cycle

In-scope processes.value: MLR rebate calculation → notice generation and mailing/e-delivery to every rebate-eligible enrollee, by State and market

In-scope systems.value: Notice template repository, batch generation log and mailing/e-delivery confirmation records

Compliance procedure documented.value: MLR Rebate Notice Audit Standard — sample size, content checklist against the CMS model notice, mailing/e-delivery timing check, finding disposition

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Audit Executive; audit program reviewed annually and on any CMS model-notice update

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rebates and notices must issue by September 30 following the MLR reporting year; the notice audit closes before that mailing window opens

Deadline reminders configured.value: Audit plan milestone alerts at T-45/T-20/T-5 days to the September 30 rebate/notice mailing deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit workpaper, sampled notices and content checklist retained 7 years from the rebate year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any notice found non-conforming to the CMS model content or mailed outside the deadline is logged as a compliance exception with root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every notice-content remediation and any late-mailing corrective mailing

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All rebate-eligible enrollee notices generated for the MLR reporting year, drawn from the notice generation batch log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on missing required CMS model-notice content elements or notices issued after September 30; any 1 fail escalates to full-batch review

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the notice audit runs once per MLR reporting year ahead of the mailing window, with a post-mailing verification pass

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed the sampled notice content review

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MLR notice audit workpaper (population extract, sample, content checklist results, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Audit report with sampled notice images and content checklist, presentable to CMS or a state MLR examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the CMS MLR examination response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a non-conforming notice before it is sent

checklist.step: Pull the current CMS model MLR rebate notice and build the content checklist
actions: Download the current CMS-prescribed model rebate notice template and the 45 CFR 158.251 required-content list.
Build a line-item checklist of every required element: MLR standard, issuer's calculated MLR, rebate amount/method, and the plain-language explanation.
Confirm the checklist against last cycle's version and note any CMS template change.
checklist.done: a content checklist mapped to 45 CFR 158.251 and the current CMS model notice exists for the audit.

checklist.step: Confirm the notice template in production matches the current CMS model
actions: Open the production notice template in OpenText Document Mgmt and compare it field-by-field to the current CMS model notice.
Flag any missing or altered required element to the Audit Analyst.
Confirm the template version number and effective date are recorded in the repository.
checklist.done: the production template is confirmed to match the current CMS model, with version and date recorded.

checklist.step: Extract the rebate-eligible enrollee population and the generated notice batch
actions: Pull the rebate-eligible enrollee list by State and market from the MLR calculation output.
Pull the corresponding notice generation batch log confirming a notice was generated for each eligible enrollee.
Reconcile the two counts and escalate any enrollee missing a generated notice to Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: the eligible population reconciles to the generated notice batch, with any gap escalated.

checklist.step: Draw and review a sample of generated notices against the content checklist
actions: Draw a sample stratified by State and market, minimum 25 notices or 10% of the batch, whichever is greater.
Score each sampled notice against every checklist line item and record pass/fail per element.
Log any failed element with the notice id and enrollee state.
checklist.done: every sampled notice is scored against the full checklist with results recorded by element.

checklist.step: Verify the rebate amount and MLR figure on the notice tie to the filed MLR report
actions: Pull the filed MLR annual report figures for the matching State and market.
Compare the MLR percentage and per-enrollee rebate amount on the sampled notice to the filed report.
Log any mismatch as a content-accuracy exception.
checklist.done: MLR percentage and rebate amount on sampled notices tie to the filed MLR report, or the mismatch is logged.

checklist.step: Check the notice delivery method against the enrollee's election on file
actions: For each sampled enrollee, confirm whether their delivery preference on file is paper or electronic.
Confirm the actual delivery channel used matches the preference on file.
Log any mismatch (e.g., e-delivery without consent) as an exception.
checklist.done: delivery channel used matches the enrollee's election on file for every sampled notice, or is logged.

checklist.step: Confirm mailing/e-delivery timing against the September 30 deadline
actions: Pull the mail-house dispatch confirmation or e-delivery send log for each sampled notice.
Compare the dispatch/send date to September 30 of the current cycle.
Log any notice dispatched after the deadline as an exception with the delay reason.
checklist.done: dispatch/send dates are confirmed on or before September 30 for every sampled notice, or logged with a delay reason.

checklist.step: Assess readability and plain-language compliance of the notice text
actions: Run the notice body text through a Flesch readability check against the plain-language standard referenced in 45 CFR 158.251 guidance.
Confirm the explanation of the MLR standard and rebate calculation avoids undefined technical jargon.
Log any readability failure for template revision.
checklist.done: the notice text passes the readability check or a template revision is logged.

checklist.step: Write up every finding with severity and required corrective action
actions: Consolidate every failed checklist element, timing miss and readability finding into the audit report.
Rate each finding's severity (content omission, timing miss, accuracy error, readability) and its enrollee impact.
Route the draft report to Chief Audit Executive for review.
checklist.done: a draft audit report with rated findings is routed to Chief Audit Executive.

checklist.step: Get management response and corrective action commitments
actions: Review each finding and provide a written management response with a corrective action and target date.
Where the finding affects notices already mailed, propose a corrective re-mailing plan.
Return the response to Audit Analyst for inclusion in the final report.
checklist.done: every finding has a management response with a corrective action and target date.

checklist.step: Execute any required corrective re-mailing
actions: Regenerate the corrected notice from the updated template for every affected enrollee.
Dispatch the corrective notice and log the new dispatch date against the original notice id.
Confirm the corrective mailing count matches the affected-enrollee count.
checklist.done: every affected enrollee has a corrective notice dispatched and logged against the original notice id.

checklist.step: Log the exception and its disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue per finding with root cause (template defect, mail-house delay, data error) and owner.
Set a remediation date and, where enrollee volume is material, assess whether a self-report to CMS is warranted.
Sign off the disposition once corrective action is confirmed complete.
checklist.done: every finding has a logged issue, root cause, owner and a signed disposition.

checklist.step: Finalize and distribute the audit report
actions: Review the draft report, findings, management responses and corrective actions for completeness.
Approve and issue the final audit report to the Audit Committee and Compliance leadership.
Set the follow-up date to verify corrective actions were completed.
checklist.done: the final audit report is issued to the Audit Committee with a scheduled corrective-action follow-up.

checklist.step: Verify corrective actions on the follow-up date
actions: On the scheduled follow-up date, confirm each corrective action's target date was met with evidence.
Close each finding in the audit tracker once verified, or extend and escalate any missed target date.
Record the closure or extension in the audit report addendum.
checklist.done: every finding is closed with verification evidence, or extended and escalated with a recorded reason.

checklist.step: Retain the audit workpaper and sampled notices
actions: Move the audit workpaper, content checklist scoring and sampled notice images into the compliance evidence repository under the rebate year.
Apply the 7-year-from-rebate-year retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by State, market and notice id.
checklist.done: the audit record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by State and market.

testing.step: Build the population of rebate-eligible enrollee notices for the year
actions: Independently extract the notice generation batch log for the rebate year from OpenText Document Mgmt.
Reconcile the extract to the rebate-eligible enrollee list from the MLR calculation output.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is independently reconciled to the MLR calculation output and signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of notices that were the subject of a corrective re-mailing.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 additional notices from the remaining population, stratified by State.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers all corrective re-mailings.

testing.step: Independently re-score each sampled notice against the CMS content checklist
actions: Read the current CMS model notice and 45 CFR 158.251 content list without reviewing the Audit Analyst's original scoring first.
Score each sampled notice pass/fail per required element independently.
Compare to the original scoring; any difference is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled notice has an independent content score compared to the original, with differences logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the rebate amount and MLR tie-out
actions: Pull the filed MLR annual report for the matching State and market for each sampled notice.
Recompute the expected rebate amount and MLR percentage shown on the notice.
Log any mismatch as an exception with the dollar difference.
testing.done: rebate amount and MLR percentage are independently recomputed and compared for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Verify dispatch timing against the September 30 deadline
actions: Pull the mail-house or e-delivery send log for each sampled notice directly from the vendor system, not the audit workpaper.
Compare the dispatch date to September 30.
Log any notice dispatched late that was not already captured as an original finding.
testing.done: dispatch timing is independently verified from the vendor system for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Confirm delivery-channel consent for the sample
actions: Pull each sampled enrollee's delivery preference record from the enrollment system.
Compare to the channel actually used, independent of the Correspondence Clerk's original check.
Log any consent mismatch not already captured as an original finding.
testing.done: delivery-channel consent is independently confirmed for every sampled notice.

testing.step: Test the corrective re-mailing evidence
actions: For every notice with a corrective re-mailing, confirm the corrective notice content passes the checklist and was dispatched.
Confirm the corrective dispatch date is within the committed corrective action target date.
Log any corrective mailing that missed its own target date.
testing.done: every corrective re-mailing is confirmed content-compliant and on time, or logged as missed.

testing.step: Confirm the self-report decision on material findings
actions: Review the finding volume and enrollee impact against the self-report threshold assessment made by Compliance Officer.
Confirm the decision rationale is documented and, where a report was filed with CMS, the filing date and confirmation.
Log any undocumented or unsupported decision as an exception.
testing.done: the self-report decision is confirmed documented and supported, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the notice id, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's audit as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on content omissions and late dispatch.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Sign the workpaper and report results to the Audit Committee and Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 45 CFR 156.410, 156.420, 147.126 / PHSA 2711 and 156.130 re-read whenever a new CMS data-call bulletin or HIOS submission window is announced

In-scope processes.value: CMS and state data-call identification → calendar entry → owner assignment → submission tracking, for every CSR/EHB-linked data call (EDGE server, RADV, QHP certification, CSR reconciliation)

In-scope systems.value: Data-call calendar entries, owner assignment fields and submission status tracking

Compliance procedure documented.value: Data Call Tracking Standard — bulletin monitoring source, calendar entry fields, owner assignment SLA, reminder cadence, escalation path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and whenever CMS revises the data-call submission calendar

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per data call — CSR-related submissions cluster around the September 30 pre-Open-Enrollment certification window; each is individually calendared from its CMS-announced date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Tracker milestone alerts at T-60/T-30/T-10 days for every open data call, plus a standing T-90 check ahead of the September 30 cluster

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Calendar snapshots, CMS bulletin captures and submission confirmations retained 7 years from the data-call year

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any data call missed from the calendar or submitted late is logged as a compliance exception with root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every missed-data-call remediation and any late-submission root-cause finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All CMS and state data-call announcements applicable to CSR/EHB in the test period, drawn from the CMS HIOS bulletin archive

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a data call absent from the calendar; any 1 miss triggers a full-period bulletin re-scan

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-data-call; test runs quarterly over that quarter's CMS bulletin population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the calendar being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly data-call tracking test workpaper (bulletin population, calendar reconciliation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar export with owner assignment and submission status, presentable to a CMS program integrity inquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the CMS inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a missed data call before it is sent

checklist.step: Monitor CMS and state bulletin sources for new data-call announcements
actions: Check the CMS CCIIO Regulations and Guidance page and the HIOS bulletin board weekly for new data-call, EDGE server or QHP certification announcements.
Check each in-scope State DOI bulletin page for state-level CSR or EHB data calls.
Log every new announcement to the intake queue with the source URL and announcement date.
checklist.done: a weekly bulletin scan is performed and every new announcement is logged to the intake queue.

checklist.step: Assess applicability of each announcement to the CSR/EHB obligation set
actions: Read each intake-queue announcement and determine whether it applies to CSR variant reporting, EHB limits or MLR/RADV data.
Mark non-applicable announcements as reviewed-and-excluded with a one-line rationale.
Route applicable announcements to calendar entry.
checklist.done: every intake-queue announcement has a documented applicability decision.

checklist.step: Create the calendar entry with all required fields
actions: In the data-call tracker, create an entry with data-call name, regulator, submission portal, format required, data elements and the CMS-announced deadline.
Attach the source bulletin capture to the entry.
Set status to 'Open — unassigned' until an owner is confirmed.
checklist.done: a complete calendar entry exists for every applicable data call with the source bulletin attached.

checklist.step: Assign a named owner to each calendar entry
actions: Assign a named data-extraction owner and a named submission owner to each open entry within 5 business days of creation.
Confirm the owner acknowledges the assignment and the deadline in the tracker.
Set status to 'Open — assigned'.
checklist.done: every open entry has an acknowledged named owner within 5 business days of creation.

checklist.step: Set milestone reminders against each deadline
actions: Configure T-60/T-30/T-10 day reminder notifications to the assigned owner and Regulatory Reporting Manager for each entry.
Confirm reminders fire correctly by checking the tracker notification log after the first milestone passes.
Add a standing T-90 reminder for any entry falling within the September 30 cluster.
checklist.done: milestone reminders are configured and confirmed firing for every open entry.

checklist.step: Cross-check the calendar against the prior year's data-call set
actions: Compare this year's calendar entries to last year's recurring data calls (EDGE server, RADV, QHP certification).
Investigate and confirm the reason for any recurring data call not yet appearing this year (genuinely discontinued vs. not yet announced).
Add a placeholder entry with a follow-up date for any expected-but-not-yet-announced data call.
checklist.done: every recurring prior-year data call is accounted for, discontinued with reason or placeholder-tracked.

checklist.step: Hand off the extraction requirements to Data Management
actions: For each assigned entry, send the Data Steward the required data elements, format and the extraction deadline (backed off the submission deadline).
Confirm the Data Steward acknowledges the extraction deadline in writing.
Record the acknowledgment date on the calendar entry.
checklist.done: every entry's extraction requirement is handed off with an acknowledged extraction deadline.

checklist.step: Track submission status through to confirmation
actions: Update the calendar entry status as the submission moves through extraction, validation and submission.
Attach the submission confirmation receipt once received from the regulator portal.
Set status to 'Closed — confirmed' only once the receipt is attached.
checklist.done: every entry reaches 'Closed — confirmed' with an attached submission confirmation.

checklist.step: Escalate any entry approaching deadline without extraction complete
actions: At the T-10 milestone, review every entry not yet at 'validation complete' status.
Escalate to the assigned owner's manager and to Compliance Officer for any entry at risk of missing the deadline.
Record the escalation and its resolution on the calendar entry.
checklist.done: every at-risk entry at T-10 has a recorded escalation and resolution.

checklist.step: Log a missed or late data call as a compliance exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any data call submitted after its CMS deadline or discovered after the fact.
Assign root cause (bulletin missed, owner unassigned, extraction delay) and an owner.
Determine whether a late-submission explanation letter to CMS is required and route to Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: every missed or late data call has a logged issue, root cause and a documented CMS-notification decision.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the CMS HIOS submission history quarterly
actions: Log in to the CMS HIOS system and pull the submission history for all data calls filed under the company's HIOS issuer id.
Compare the HIOS history to the calendar's 'Closed — confirmed' entries for the same period.
Investigate and resolve any entry present in one system but not the other.
checklist.done: the calendar reconciles quarterly to the CMS HIOS submission history with discrepancies resolved.

checklist.step: Review the calendar and process at the annual cycle refresh
actions: Review the full-year calendar for missed entries, late submissions and escalation patterns.
Approve any change to the bulletin monitoring sources or reminder cadence for the next cycle.
Sign the annual procedure re-approval.
checklist.done: the annual calendar review is complete with a signed procedure re-approval.

checklist.step: Publish the rolling calendar to affected stakeholders
actions: Publish a rolling 12-month view of open and upcoming data calls to the Compliance and Data Management Confluence space.
Update the published view whenever a new entry is created or a deadline changes.
Confirm stakeholders acknowledge visibility at the monthly Compliance sync.
checklist.done: a current rolling 12-month calendar view is published and stakeholder-acknowledged monthly.

checklist.step: Confirm no CSR/EHB data call bypassed the tracker via direct regulator request
actions: Ask Regulatory Reporting Manager quarterly whether any ad hoc CMS or state request was received outside the bulletin monitoring process.
Confirm any such ad hoc request was retroactively logged as a calendar entry.
Log a gap as an exception if the ad hoc request was not tracked.
checklist.done: every ad hoc regulator request in the quarter is confirmed retroactively logged, or the gap is exceptioned.

checklist.step: Retain the calendar snapshot and bulletin evidence
actions: Export a quarterly calendar snapshot and the source bulletin captures into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-data-call-year retention label.
Confirm the snapshot is retrievable by data-call name and year.
checklist.done: quarterly calendar snapshots and bulletin evidence are filed, retention-labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of applicable CMS/state data-call announcements for the quarter
actions: Independently pull the CMS CCIIO/HIOS bulletin archive and relevant State DOI bulletin pages for the quarter.
Identify every announcement applicable to CSR/EHB reporting using the same applicability criteria as the process.
Reconcile this independently built population to the intake queue log.
testing.done: an independently built bulletin population is reconciled to the intake queue log.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of announcements not found in the calendar tracker.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 additional entries from the calendared population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all untracked announcements plus a documented random sample of tracked entries.

testing.step: Verify each sampled announcement has a complete calendar entry
actions: Open the tracker entry for each sampled announcement and confirm all required fields are populated.
Confirm the deadline recorded matches the CMS-announced deadline in the source bulletin.
Log any missing field or deadline mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled entry is confirmed complete and accurate against the source bulletin, or logged.

testing.step: Confirm owner assignment timing for the sample
actions: Compare the entry creation date to the owner acknowledgment date for each sampled entry.
Confirm assignment occurred within the 5-business-day standard.
Log any late assignment as an exception.
testing.done: owner assignment timing is confirmed within standard for every sampled entry, or logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the HIOS reconciliation for the sample
actions: Independently pull the CMS HIOS submission history for each sampled entry's data call.
Compare submission date and confirmation status to what is recorded in the tracker.
Log any discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: HIOS submission history is independently confirmed against the tracker for every sampled entry.

testing.step: Test reminder and escalation evidence for the sample
actions: Pull the tracker notification log for each sampled entry and confirm T-60/T-30/T-10 reminders fired.
For any entry that reached T-10 without validation complete, confirm an escalation was recorded.
Log any missing reminder or unescalated at-risk entry as an exception.
testing.done: reminder firing and escalation are confirmed for every sampled entry, or logged.

testing.step: Verify prior-year recurring data-call continuity
actions: Compare the current year's calendared recurring data calls to the prior year's closed entries.
Confirm every recurring call either appears this year or has a documented discontinuation reason.
Log any silently dropped recurring data call as an exception.
testing.done: recurring data-call continuity is confirmed year-over-year, with any silent drop logged.

testing.step: Check ad hoc regulator request tracking
actions: Interview Regulatory Reporting Manager and review email/correspondence logs for any direct CMS or state request during the quarter.
Confirm every such request has a corresponding retroactive calendar entry.
Log any untracked ad hoc request as an exception.
testing.done: ad hoc regulator requests for the quarter are confirmed tracked, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the data-call name, what was missed and the compliance impact.

checklist.step: Map the CMS MLR form's required data elements to source systems
actions: Open the current CMS MLR Annual Reporting Form instructions and list every required data element: earned premium, incurred claims, quality-improvement activity expense, taxes and fees, by State and market.
For each element, identify the source system of record (general ledger account, claims platform field, tax sub-ledger).
Publish the element-to-source mapping to the Data Engineering team.
checklist.done: a complete data-element-to-source mapping exists for every field on the current CMS MLR form.

checklist.step: Build or refresh the extraction queries for each source system
actions: Write or update the extraction pipeline pulling earned premium and tax data from the general ledger by State/market/product cost center.
Write or update the extraction pipeline pulling incurred claims (paid plus reserve movement) from the claims platform by State/market.
Load the extracts into the MLR data mart and log the extraction run id and row counts.
checklist.done: extraction pipelines run successfully for every required element with logged run ids and row counts.

checklist.step: Extract quality-improvement activity expense with supporting detail
actions: Pull quality-improvement activity expense from the designated GL cost centers per the CMS QIA expense definition.
Confirm each expense line has a description supporting its QIA classification, not a general administrative cost.
Flag any expense lacking QIA-qualifying support for Controller review.
checklist.done: QIA expense is extracted with supporting classification detail, and unsupported items are flagged.

checklist.step: Reconcile extracted premium and claims totals to the general ledger
actions: In the data catalog/quality tool, run the reconciliation rule comparing MLR data mart totals to the general ledger trial balance by State/market.
Investigate and document the cause of any difference above the materiality threshold set by Controller.
Record the reconciliation result and any adjusting entry on the validation report.
checklist.done: MLR data mart totals reconcile to the general ledger by State/market, with differences documented.

checklist.step: Run completeness and range validation rules on every element
actions: Run null/completeness checks confirming every State/market combination has a populated value for every required element.
Run range and outlier checks (e.g., negative claims, premium below zero) and flag any failure.
Log each rule's pass/fail result to the validation report.
checklist.done: completeness and range validation results are recorded for every required element.

checklist.step: Validate claims incurred-but-not-reported reserve treatment
actions: Confirm the incurred claims extract includes the IBNR reserve movement consistent with the statutory annual statement.
Compare the MLR incurred-claims figure to the corresponding Schedule H / health annual statement exhibit line.
Log any inconsistency for Controller resolution before handoff.
checklist.done: incurred claims including IBNR reconcile to the statutory annual statement exhibit.

checklist.step: Resolve every validation failure before handoff
actions: Review every failed completeness, range or reconciliation rule from the validation report.
Correct the extraction logic or source data and re-run the failed rule.
Confirm all rules pass or are formally waived with a documented reason and Controller sign-off.
checklist.done: every validation rule passes or carries a documented, signed waiver before handoff.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller sign-off on the validated data set
actions: Review the validation report, reconciliation results and any waivers.
Confirm the data set is ready for the CMS MLR form population.
Sign the data-set approval field on the validation report.
checklist.done: Controller signs the validation report before the data set is released for form population.

checklist.step: Hand off the validated data set to Regulatory Reporting
actions: Package the validated MLR data mart extract with the signed validation report.
Deliver the package to Regulatory Reporting Analyst with enough lead time for form population, review and submission before July 31.
Confirm receipt is acknowledged in writing.
checklist.done: the validated data package is handed off to Regulatory Reporting with an acknowledged receipt date.

checklist.step: Track the handoff date against the internal lead-time target
actions: Log the handoff date on the data-call tracker entry for the MLR report.
Compare the handoff date to the internal target date backed off July 31.
Escalate to Chief Data Officer any handoff at risk of missing the target.
checklist.done: the handoff date is logged and compared to the internal target, with at-risk handoffs escalated.

checklist.step: Support Regulatory Reporting through form-level queries
actions: Respond to Regulatory Reporting's field-level questions on the data set within 1 business day.
Correct and re-validate any element found inconsistent with the CMS form's line-item definitions during review.
Log each correction and its re-validation result.
checklist.done: form-level queries from Regulatory Reporting are resolved within 1 business day with logged corrections.

checklist.step: Log every validation exception with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any validation failure that required a waiver or a late correction.
Assign root cause (source data quality, mapping error, timing) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm it is tracked for the next reporting year's extraction build.
checklist.done: every validation exception has a logged issue, root cause, owner and next-year remediation tracking.

checklist.step: Review data lineage documentation for audit readiness
actions: Confirm the data catalog shows lineage from each MLR form field back to its general ledger account or claims platform field.
Confirm the lineage documentation is current for the reporting year's extraction logic.
Sign off the lineage documentation as audit-ready.
checklist.done: current, audit-ready data lineage exists from every MLR form field to its source.

checklist.step: Archive the extraction queries and validation report
actions: Version and archive the extraction query set used for the reporting year.
Move the validation report and reconciliation workpapers into the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year.
Apply the 7-year-from-reporting-year retention label.
checklist.done: the extraction queries and validation report are versioned, filed and retention-labelled.

checklist.step: Debrief and update the extraction/validation standard for next cycle
actions: Review the cycle's exceptions, waivers and handoff timing against the target.
Approve any update to the extraction pipeline, validation rule set or lead-time target for next year.
Sign the annual standard re-approval.
checklist.done: the annual debrief is complete with a signed re-approval of the extraction/validation standard.

testing.step: Build the population of MLR data elements extracted for the reporting year
actions: Independently pull the MLR data mart extract for the reporting year by State and market.
Reconcile the extract's row counts to the extraction run log maintained by Data Engineering.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is independently reconciled to the extraction run log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of State/market combinations that carried a validation waiver.
Take a seeded random sample of 15 additional State/market combinations from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all waived combinations plus a documented random sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the general ledger reconciliation for the sample
actions: Independently pull the general ledger trial balance for each sampled State/market and compare to the MLR data mart total.
Recompute the difference and compare to the materiality threshold used in the original reconciliation.
Log any unexplained or newly identified difference as an exception.
testing.done: the general ledger reconciliation is independently reproduced for every sampled combination.

testing.step: Re-run completeness and range validation rules on the sample
actions: Independently re-run the completeness and range checks against the sampled data using the documented rule definitions.
Compare the results to the original validation report.
Log any rule that fails independently but passed the original run as an exception.
testing.done: validation rules are independently re-run and compared to the original results for the sample.

testing.step: Trace incurred claims to the statutory annual statement exhibit
actions: For each sampled State/market, pull the incurred claims figure from the Schedule H / health annual statement exhibit.
Compare to the MLR data mart's incurred claims figure including IBNR movement.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: incurred claims are traced to the statutory exhibit and reconciled for every sampled combination.

testing.step: Test QIA expense classification support
actions: Pull the supporting detail for sampled QIA expense line items from the general ledger.
Assess each against the CMS QIA expense definition for genuine quality-improvement qualification.
Log any misclassified expense as an exception with the dollar impact.
testing.done: QIA expense classification is independently assessed and any misclassification logged.

testing.step: Verify data lineage for the sample
actions: Open the data catalog lineage view for each sampled element and trace it back to its general ledger account or claims field.
Confirm the lineage matches the documented mapping used in the extraction pipeline.
Log any broken or undocumented lineage as an exception.
testing.done: lineage is independently verified for every sampled element, or logged as broken.

testing.step: Confirm handoff timing against the internal lead-time target
actions: Pull the logged handoff date and Regulatory Reporting's acknowledged receipt date from the tracker.
Compare to the internal target date backed off July 31.
Log any handoff that missed its target as an exception.
testing.done: handoff timing is confirmed against the target for the reporting year, or logged as missed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the State/market, element and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on unreconciled elements reaching the form.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.
