checklist.step: Receive the validated MLR data set and confirm completeness
actions: Receive the validated data package and Controller-signed validation report from Data Steward.
Confirm every State and market required to report has a complete row in the data set.
Escalate to Regulatory Reporting Manager any State/market missing from the handoff.
checklist.done: the validated data package is confirmed complete for every required State/market before form population.

checklist.step: Populate the CMS MLR Annual Reporting Form
actions: Map each validated data element into the corresponding line of the CMS MLR Annual Reporting Form template in the internal staging system.
Populate premium, claims, quality-improvement, tax and credibility-adjustment fields exactly per the CMS form instructions for each State/market.
Run the internal cross-footing check confirming subtotals and totals calculate correctly.
checklist.done: the form is fully populated for every State/market with a passing cross-footing check.

checklist.step: Perform a first-line review of the populated form
actions: Compare each populated field back to the source validated data set line by line for a sample of State/market rows.
Confirm rebate calculation logic and credibility adjustment factors match the CMS-prescribed methodology.
Log any discrepancy found and correct before escalating for second-line review.
checklist.done: a first-line line-by-line review is complete with discrepancies corrected.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller review and sign-off of the populated form
actions: Review the populated form's premium, claims and tax figures against the general ledger and the validation report.
Confirm the rebate calculation ties to the actuarial/finance rebate workpaper.
Sign the form review approval before it proceeds to submission.
checklist.done: Controller signs the form review approval before submission.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Financial Officer final sign-off before submission
actions: Review the Controller-approved form summary and the total rebate liability across all States/markets.
Confirm the submission is ready and authorize release to the HHS MLR reporting system.
Sign the final submission authorization.
checklist.done: Chief Financial Officer signs the final submission authorization.

checklist.step: Submit the form through the HHS MLR Annual Reporting System
actions: Log in to the HHS MLR Annual Reporting System with the company's authorized user credentials.
Upload or key the authorized form data for each State/market and submit before the July 31 deadline.
Download and save the system-generated submission confirmation number and timestamp for each State/market.
checklist.done: the form is submitted for every State/market before July 31 with a saved confirmation number and timestamp.

checklist.step: Verify the submission was accepted, not just transmitted
actions: Log back in to the HHS MLR reporting system 1 business day after submission and check each State/market's status.
Confirm status shows Accepted, not Pending or Rejected.
Escalate any Rejected or stuck-Pending status to Regulatory Reporting Manager immediately.
checklist.done: every State/market submission shows an Accepted status confirmed the next business day.

checklist.step: Reconcile the submitted form to the validated source data
actions: Compare the final submitted form values to the validated data set for every State/market.
Confirm no manual edit was made during submission that was not reflected back in the source data set.
Log any unreconciled difference for Controller review.
checklist.done: submitted form values reconcile to the validated source data set for every State/market.

checklist.step: Log the submission receipt in the data-call tracker
actions: Attach the confirmation number, timestamp and accepted-status screenshot to the MLR data-call tracker entry.
Set the tracker entry status to 'Closed — confirmed'.
Notify Compliance Officer that the annual submission cycle is complete.
checklist.done: the tracker entry is closed with confirmation evidence attached and Compliance notified.

checklist.step: Escalate any submission at risk of missing the July 31 deadline
actions: At the T-3 milestone, review any State/market not yet submitted.
Escalate to Chief Financial Officer for immediate resolution, including whether a good-faith partial submission or extension request is warranted.
Record the escalation decision and outcome on the tracker entry.
checklist.done: every at-risk submission at T-3 has a recorded escalation decision and outcome.

checklist.step: Handle any rejected submission through resubmission
actions: Read the rejection reason code returned by the HHS MLR reporting system.
Correct the identified field in the staging system and re-route for the applicable sign-off level based on the field changed.
Resubmit and confirm the new confirmation number and Accepted status.
checklist.done: every rejected submission is corrected, re-approved as needed, resubmitted and confirmed Accepted.

checklist.step: Log a late or rejected submission as a compliance exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any submission accepted after July 31 or requiring resubmission.
Assign root cause and owner, and determine whether a written explanation to CMS is warranted.
Sign off the disposition once resolved.
checklist.done: every late or rejected submission has a logged issue, root cause, owner and signed disposition.

checklist.step: Communicate the rebate obligation outcome to Finance and Actuarial
actions: Distribute the final submitted rebate figures by State/market to Controller and Appointed Actuary.
Confirm the rebate liability is booked in the general ledger consistent with the submitted form.
Trigger the rebate notice generation process for any State/market with a rebate due.
checklist.done: final rebate figures are distributed, booked and the notice process is triggered where a rebate is due.

checklist.step: Retain the submission package for the retention period
actions: Move the populated form, all sign-offs and the HHS confirmation receipts into the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year.
Apply the 7-year-from-reporting-year retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by State, market and confirmation number.
checklist.done: the submission package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by State and confirmation number.

checklist.step: Debrief the submission cycle and update the standard for next year
actions: Review the cycle's timeline, escalations and any rejection root causes.
Approve any change to the review-and-sign-off sequence or submission timeline for next year.
Sign the annual standard re-approval.
checklist.done: the annual debrief is complete with a signed re-approval of the submission standard.

testing.step: Build the population of State/market MLR submissions for the reporting year
actions: Independently pull the list of confirmation numbers and submission timestamps from the HHS MLR reporting system for the reporting year.
Reconcile the list to the data-call tracker's 'Closed — confirmed' entries.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is independently reconciled to the HHS system's own confirmation list.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method

Take a seeded random sample of 15 additional State/market submissions from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all late/rejected submissions plus a documented random sample.

testing.step: Verify submission timing against the July 31 deadline
actions: For each sampled State/market, pull the submission timestamp directly from the HHS MLR reporting system, not the internal tracker.
Compare the timestamp to July 31 of the reporting year.
Log any submission after the deadline not already captured as an original exception.
testing.done: submission timing is independently verified from the HHS system for every sampled State/market.

testing.step: Reconcile the sampled submitted form values to the validated source data
actions: Pull the final submitted form values for each sampled State/market and compare to the validated data set line by line.
Recompute the rebate calculation independently and compare to the submitted figure.
Log any mismatch as an exception with the dollar difference.
testing.done: submitted values and the rebate calculation are independently reconciled for every sampled State/market.

testing.step: Confirm sign-off sequence and authorization for the sample
actions: Pull the review and sign-off trail (first-line, Controller, Chief Financial Officer) for each sampled submission.
Confirm every sign-off pre-dates the actual submission timestamp.
Log any submission made without a complete, pre-dated sign-off chain as an exception.
testing.done: the sign-off chain is confirmed complete and pre-dated for every sampled submission, or logged.

actions: For every sampled rejected submission, pull the rejection reason code and the corrected field.
Confirm the resubmission carried the appropriate re-approval based on the field changed.
Confirm the final Accepted confirmation number and timestamp are on file.
testing.done: rejection handling and resubmission are confirmed appropriately re-approved and accepted for every sampled case.

testing.step: Trace the rebate liability booking to the general ledger

Compare the booked amount to the final submitted form's rebate figure.
Log any unbooked or mismatched liability as an exception.
testing.done: the rebate liability booking is traced and confirmed to match the submitted figure for the sample.

testing.step: Confirm rebate notice triggering for sampled rebate-due State/markets
actions: Confirm the notice generation process was triggered for every sampled State/market with a rebate due.
Cross-reference to the notice generation batch log tested under the notice audit item.
Log any State/market with a rebate due but no triggered notice as an exception.
testing.done: notice triggering is confirmed for every sampled rebate-due State/market, or logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the State/market, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next reporting year's test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on late submissions.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Consolidate rejection/edit-failure queues across all ACA/PHSA data channels
actions: Connect the 834 enrollment processor's edit-failure queue, the CMS EDGE server rejection report, the MLR staging system's validation failures and the QHP certification portal's error list into a single monitoring view.
Confirm each source feeds the consolidated view within 1 hour of the rejection occurring.
Tag each item with its source channel and rejection code.
checklist.done: a consolidated, tagged rejection queue exists covering every in-scope channel, refreshing within 1 hour.

checklist.step: Triage each new rejection within 1 business day
actions: Open each new queue item and read the channel-specific rejection/edit-failure code and description.
Assign an initial root-cause category: source data error, mapping/transformation defect, timing/sequencing issue, or regulator-side portal issue.
Assign an owner and set the resubmission window based on the source channel's own rules.
checklist.done: every new rejection is triaged with a root-cause category, owner and resubmission window within 1 business day.

checklist.step: Investigate a source-data-error rejection at the record level
actions: Pull the specific member or transaction record cited in the rejection from its system of record (enrollment, claims, GL).
Compare the rejected value to the source record and identify the specific field causing the failure.
Determine whether the source system holds a data-entry error requiring correction at the source, not just the extract.
checklist.done: every source-data-error rejection is traced to a specific field and source-record finding.

checklist.step: Investigate a mapping/transformation-defect rejection against the pipeline logic
actions: Open the extraction/transformation pipeline step that produced the rejected field and compare its logic to the channel's current edit-check specification.
Identify whether the specification changed (e.g., a new CMS EDGE server edit) without a corresponding pipeline update.
Draft the pipeline fix and route it for peer review before deployment.
checklist.done: every mapping/transformation rejection is traced to a specific pipeline step with a drafted fix.

checklist.step: Correct the underlying record or field
actions: Apply the correction at the source system for a source-data-error root cause, or confirm the pipeline fix deployment for a mapping-defect root cause.
Re-run the affected record through the extraction/validation pipeline to confirm the field now passes.
Record the correction detail and re-validation result on the queue item.
checklist.done: the correction is applied at the appropriate layer and the record passes re-validation.

checklist.step: Resubmit the corrected transaction through the originating channel
actions: Log in to the originating channel (834 processor resubmission queue, CMS EDGE server portal, MLR staging system, or QHP certification portal) with the corrected record.
Submit the correction within the channel's resubmission window and capture the new confirmation number or accepted-status timestamp.
Attach the confirmation to the queue item.
checklist.done: the corrected transaction is resubmitted within the channel's window with a captured confirmation.

checklist.step: Verify the resubmission cleared the original rejection
actions: Check the originating channel's status for the resubmitted record shows Accepted, not a repeat rejection.
For a repeat rejection, re-open the queue item and escalate to Data Engineer for deeper root-cause analysis.
Close the queue item only on a confirmed Accepted status.
checklist.done: the queue item is closed only after the originating channel confirms Accepted status.

checklist.step: Escalate any rejection approaching its resubmission window without resolution
actions: Review the queue-age report daily and identify items within 1 day of their channel's resubmission window.
Escalate unresolved items to the assigned owner's manager and to Compliance Officer.
Record the escalation and the resulting action on the queue item.
checklist.done: every item approaching its resubmission window without resolution has a recorded escalation.

checklist.step: Identify and act on recurring root causes
actions: Run a weekly aggregation of closed rejections by root-cause category and source channel.
Flag any root cause recurring 3 or more times in a rolling 30-day window.
Open a permanent-fix initiative for any flagged recurring root cause rather than continuing to correct case-by-case.
checklist.done: recurring root causes are identified weekly and a permanent-fix initiative is opened for any flagged pattern.

checklist.step: Track a permanent fix for a recurring root cause to deployment
actions: Open a change ticket for the permanent pipeline or source-system fix addressing the recurring root cause.
Test the fix against a sample of previously rejected records to confirm it resolves the pattern.
Deploy the fix and confirm the recurring rejection stops appearing in the following cycle.
checklist.done: a permanent fix for the recurring root cause is deployed and confirmed to stop the pattern.

checklist.step: Log every rejection exceeding its resubmission window as a compliance exception
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any rejection closed after its resubmission window, or any recurring root cause flagged twice.
Assign root cause and owner, and determine whether the delay caused a downstream regulator-facing miss (e.g., a late MLR figure).
Set a remediation date and sign off once resolved.
checklist.done: every window-breaching or recurring-pattern rejection has a logged issue, root cause, owner and signed disposition.

checklist.step: Confirm downstream regulator-facing figures were corrected where affected
actions: For any rejection that fed into an already-submitted regulator report, determine whether the correction changes the previously reported figure.
Where it does, initiate the applicable amendment or resubmission process with the regulator.
Record the amendment decision and its outcome.
checklist.done: every rejection affecting an already-submitted report has a recorded amendment decision and outcome.

checklist.step: Publish the weekly rejection-queue status to Data Management and Compliance
actions: Publish open/closed counts, average time-to-close and recurring root-cause trends by channel in the Power BI data-quality dashboard.
Distribute the dashboard link to Data Management and Compliance leadership weekly.
Highlight any channel with a rising rejection rate for the monthly Compliance sync.
checklist.done: a weekly rejection-queue status dashboard is published and distributed.

checklist.step: Review the resolution standard and channel-specific SLAs annually
actions: Review the year's rejection volume, escalations and recurring-fix outcomes by channel.
Approve any change to the triage SLA or resubmission-window tracking for the next cycle.
Sign the annual standard re-approval.
checklist.done: the annual review is complete with a signed re-approval of the resolution standard.

checklist.step: Retain the rejection and resolution evidence
actions: Move the closed queue item detail, root-cause finding and resubmission confirmation into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year-from-resolution retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by source channel and rejection code.
checklist.done: closed rejection records are filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by channel and rejection code.

testing.step: Build the population of rejection/edit-failure queue items for the quarter
actions: Extract every queue item opened in the quarter across all in-scope channels from the consolidated monitoring view.
Reconcile the extract to each source channel's own rejection report (834 processor, EDGE server, MLR staging, QHP portal) for the same period.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to each source channel's own rejection report and signed as complete.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of items that breached their resubmission window or were flagged as a recurring root cause.
Take a seeded random sample of 20 additional items from the remaining population, stratified by channel.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers all window breaches and recurring flags plus a documented random sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the triage classification for each sampled rejection
actions: Read the rejection code and description for each sampled item without reviewing the original root-cause assignment first.
Independently classify the root cause and compare to the original classification.
Log any difference as an exception, including a misclassification that hid a recurring pattern.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent root-cause classification compared to the original.

testing.step: Trace the correction and resubmission for each sampled rejection
actions: Pull the correction detail and the resubmission confirmation for each sampled item directly from the originating channel.
Confirm the resubmission timestamp falls within the channel's resubmission window.
Log any resubmission missing, late, or unconfirmed as an exception.
testing.done: correction and resubmission are independently traced and timing confirmed for every sampled item.

testing.step: Verify closure status against the originating channel
actions: For each sampled closed item, check the originating channel's live status directly, not the queue item's recorded status.
Confirm the channel shows Accepted, not a repeat or unresolved rejection.
Log any item closed in the queue but not actually accepted by the channel as an exception.
testing.done: closure status is independently confirmed against the originating channel for every sampled item.

testing.step: Test escalation evidence for window-breaching items
actions: For each sampled item that breached its resubmission window, pull the escalation record.
Confirm the escalation occurred at the 1-day-remaining threshold as required.
Log any missing or late escalation as an exception.
testing.done: escalation timing is confirmed for every sampled window-breaching item, or logged as missed.

testing.step: Verify recurring-root-cause detection and permanent-fix deployment
actions: Independently rebuild the 30-day rolling root-cause aggregation for the sampled channels.
Compare to the flagged recurring patterns and confirm a permanent-fix ticket was opened for each.
Confirm the permanent fix was tested against previously rejected records before deployment.
testing.done: recurring-pattern detection and permanent-fix deployment are independently verified for the sample.

testing.step: Check downstream regulator-report amendment decisions
actions: For sampled rejections that fed an already-submitted regulator report, review the amendment decision and rationale.
Confirm the decision is documented and, where an amendment was filed, the filing date and confirmation.
Log any undocumented decision as an exception.
testing.done: amendment decisions for sampled downstream-affecting rejections are confirmed documented, or logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the channel, rejection code and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold on unescalated window breaches.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper and report results to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.
